cells.gaps: No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months to the as-at: the only plan fact (RWA-020, plan:none) is dated 2021 and no row states finance, so the cap holds. The 100% is a rollout statement with no numerator, resting on 13 facility visits; whether the 1,250 health posts key their own reports is not established, the newest tier fact (RWA-024, 2024-06) names no T4, and reporting completeness is held only undated (RWA-011). Nothing is held for the last twelve months.
cells.note: Coverage reaches 4: reports are keyed into DHIS2 at the facility (RWA-026) and were held for all 520 primary health facilities (RWA-002); it is not 5 because no measured share of clinics entering their own data is published. The cap brings it to 3, the ministry being owner with neither a current plan nor a domestic budget line on record.

cells.gaps: No row establishes a unique patient identifier or a record retrievable at another facility, so `shared` is not met; the one digitised fact outside the excluded source (RWA-001) is dated 2026-10-01, a day after the as-at, and gives no facility count. The clinic figures disagree: 33.0% of sampled health centres using an EMR in 2023 (RWA-018), 'majority of public health facilities' with no figure in April 2026 (RWA-004), and 'more than two thirds of health centres' in September 2026 (RWA-021), which has no numerator, denominator or source and says where eBuzima is, not who enters data. T2 rests on the 2023 survey of all 42 district hospitals (RWA-019); T1 on one hospital. Rows RWA-007 to RWA-010 are from the excluded source and set nothing. Where the record is keyed is stated only by a fact dated after the as-at (RWA-001).
cells.note: Stage 3 is met on all 42 district hospitals using an EMR in 2023 and health centres using one across the country. It is not 4 because the record is not shown to be shared across facilities and the more-than-half figure for health centres is an unsourced deployment statement.
